bookInfo.name: Old History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Xue Juzheng et al.

title.zh: 卷二十 梁書20: 列傳十 謝瞳 司馬鄴 劉捍 王敬蕘 高劭 馬嗣勳 張存敬 寇彥卿
title.en: Volume 20 Book of Later Liang 20: Biographies 10 - Xie Tong, Si Maye, Liu Han, Wang Jinrao, Gao Shao, Ma Sixun, Zhang Cunjin, Kou Yanqing
title.raw: 卷二十 梁書20: 列傳十 謝瞳 司馬鄴 劉捍 王敬蕘 高劭 馬嗣勳 張存敬 寇彥卿 Volume 20 Book of Later Liang 20: Biographies 10 - Xie Tong, Si Maye, Liu Han, Wang Jinrao, Gao Shao, Ma Sixun, Zhang Cunjin, Kou Yanqing

sentences.zh: 謝瞳，字子明，福州人。

translations.literal: Xie Tong, styled Ziming, was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tong, who styled himself Ziming, came from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐咸通末舉進士，因留長安，三歲不中第。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang Xiantong he passed the jinshi examination and remained in Chang'an; three years he failed to place.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xiantong he took the jinshi degree and stayed in Chang'an; three years passed without his name on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 廣明初，黃巢陷長安，遂投跡於太祖，洎居門下，未嘗一日不在左右。

translations.literal: Early Guangming, Huang Chao took Chang'an; he then cast his lot with the Founder, and once under his gate never a day was absent from his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao seized Chang'an in the first year of Guangming, Tong entered the Founder's service and from that day was never far from his side.

sentences.zh: 及太祖據同州，遂署右職。

translations.literal: When the Founder held Tong Prefecture, he then appointed him to a right-hand post.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Founder held Tongzhou, he gave Tong a chief post on his staff.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，太祖與河中交戰，再不利，連上章請兵於巢，偽右軍都尉孟楷抑而不進。

translations.literal: That autumn the Founder fought Hezhong and twice met ill fortune; repeatedly he sent memorials asking troops of Chao, but the false Right Army commissioner Meng Kai suppressed them and they did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, twice beaten fighting Hezhong, the Founder pleaded again and again to Chao for reinforcements, but the rebel Right Army commissioner Meng Kai blocked every dispatch.

sentences.zh: 瞳揣太祖有擇福意，乃進說曰：「黃家以數十萬之師，值唐朝久安，人不習戰，因利乘便，遂下兩京。

translations.literal: Tong gauged that the Founder intended to choose fortune, and thereupon advanced counsel, saying: "The Huang house with an army of hundreds of thousands, encountering the Tang's long peace and men unpractised in war, rode advantage and seized both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Founder's wish to change sides, Tong urged him: "Huang's army of hundreds of thousands took both capitals only because the Tang had grown soft in long peace and men had forgotten war.

sentences.zh: 然始竊偽號，任用已失其所。

translations.literal: Yet having first stolen a false title, their appointments already miss their place.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the moment they claimed an emperor's title, every appointment went wrong.

sentences.zh: 今將軍勇冠三軍，力戰於外，而孟楷專務壅蔽，奏章不達，下為庸才所製，無獨斷之明，破亡之兆必矣。

translations.literal: Now the general's courage crowns the three armies, fighting hard abroad, yet Meng Kai devotes himself to blocking; memorials do not arrive, below he is constrained by mediocrities and lacks the clarity of sole decision—the omen of ruin is sure.
translations.idiomatic: You fight abroad with unmatched courage while Meng Kai chokes every letter to court; mediocrities below him run the show, and without firm command ruin is certain.

sentences.zh: 況土德未厭，外兵四集，漕運波注，日以收復為名，惟將軍察之。

translations.literal: Moreover earth's virtue is not yet spent; armies gather from four sides, grain-ships pour in waves, day by day they march under the name of restoration—only let the general consider it.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate still favors the Tang: armies close from every quarter, grain fleets pour in, and every day another force marches to restore the throne—think on that, General.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「我意素決，爾又如是，復何疑哉！

translations.literal: " The Founder said: "My mind was long settled; you speak thus too—what doubt remains!
translations.idiomatic: " The Founder replied, "My mind was made long ago; hearing you say the same, what doubt could remain?

sentences.zh: 」翌日，遂定策，戮偽監軍使，悉眾歸順於河中。

translations.literal: " The next day he settled strategy, killed the false army supervisor, and with all his host submitted to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: " Next day the plan was fixed: the false inspector was killed, and the whole army went over to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 王重榮表瞳為檢校屯田員外郎，賜緋，令奉表於蜀。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong memorialized Tong as acting Director of Palace Farms, granted him crimson robes, and ordered him to present a memorial in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong made Tong acting Director of the Palace Farms, dressed him in crimson, and sent him to present the submission to Shu.

sentences.zh: 唐僖宗大悅，召入顧問，錫賚甚厚，以功授朝散大夫、太子率更令，賜紫，為陵州刺史。

translations.literal: Tang Emperor Xizong was greatly pleased, summoned him for consultation, bestowed gifts very generously, and for merit appointed him Grand Master of the Palace, Crown Prince's Director of Water Clocks, granted purple, and made him prefect of Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong rejoiced, called him in for counsel, heaped gifts upon him, and for his service made him Grand Master of the Palace and Director of the Crown Prince's water clocks, clothed him in purple, and gave him Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 治郡一歲，改檢校右散騎常侍、通州刺史。

translations.literal: He governed the prefecture one year, then was changed to acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and prefect of Tong.
translations.idiomatic: After one year as prefect he was promoted to acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and made governor of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 在任四考，頗有政績。

translations.literal: In office through four evaluations, he had quite administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Four terms in office won him a solid record of good rule.

sentences.zh: 秋罷，詣蜀行在，太祖遣人迎之。

translations.literal: Autumn dismissed, he went to the Shu traveling court; the Founder sent men to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn brought his term to an end, he went to the imperial camp in Shu, and the Founder sent escorts to meet him.

sentences.zh: 龍紀二年，至東京，勞徠彌厚，賜第墅各一區，錢千緡，表為亳州團練使兼太清宮副使，加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: Longji year 2, he reached the Eastern Capital; rewards and comfort were thicker still, granted one ward each of mansion and villa, a thousand strings of cash, memorialized as Bozhou regimental commissioner and vice-director of the Grand Pure Palace, added acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Longji 2 he reached the Eastern Capital; the Founder received him with exceptional honors—a mansion, a country villa, a thousand strings of cash—and memorialized him Bozhou regimental commissioner and deputy head of the Grand Pure Palace, with acting rank as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，太祖征淮南，過郡，因求侍府幕，表為宣義軍節度副使，充兩使留後。

translations.literal: That winter the Founder campaigned against Huainan, passed through his prefecture; he therefore asked to serve in the commandery staff, was memorialized as vice-commissioner of the Xuanyi army and acting regent for both commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, as the Founder marched on Huainan and passed through his circuit, Tong asked to join his staff and was made vice-commissioner of the Xuanyi army and regent for both civil and military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 瞳在滑十三年，部內增戶約五萬，益兵數千人，累遷至大中大夫、檢校右僕射，卒於滑。

translations.literal: Tong was at Hua thirteen years; within his circuit households increased by about fifty thousand, troops increased by several thousand; he rose in succession to Grand Master and acting Right Vice Director, and died at Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years at Hua added fifty thousand households and several thousand troops to his circuit; he rose to Grand Master and acting Right Vice Director, and died there.

sentences.zh: 開平初，追贈司徒。

translations.literal: Early Kaiping he was posthumously given Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Kaiping he was posthumously named Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 司馬鄴，字表仁，其先河內溫人也。

translations.literal: Si Maye, styled Biaoren, his ancestors were men of Wen in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Si Maye, who styled himself Biaoren, came of a family from Wen in Henei.

sentences.zh: 祖德璋，仕唐為杞王傅。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dezang served Tang as tutor to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dezang had served the Tang as tutor to the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 父諲，左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Yin was Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin held the post of Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 鄴資蔭出身，頗知書，累官至大列。

translations.literal: Maye entered office by hereditary privilege, knew books quite well, and rose in office to Grand Array.
translations.idiomatic: Maye entered service by yin privilege, was well read, and rose to Grand Array.

sentences.zh: 唐天復初，韓建用為同州節度留後。

translations.literal: Early Tang Tianfu, Han Jian employed him as Tongzhou military regent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianfu, Han Jian made him acting military commissioner of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 韓建傳判官司鄴昭宗之幸鳳翔也，太祖引兵入關，前鋒至左馮翊，鄴持印鑰迎謁道左。

translations.literal: Si Maye had been Han Jian's administrative officer; when Zhaozong went to Fengxiang the Founder led troops into the Pass, the vanguard reaching Left Fengyi; Maye holding seal and keys welcomed him by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Maye had served as Han Jian's administrative officer; when Zhaozong fled to Fengxiang and the Founder entered the Pass, Maye met the vanguard at Fengyi with seal and keys in hand.

sentences.zh: 太祖以兵圍華州，命入城招諭韓建，建果出降。

translations.literal: The Founder with troops besieged Hua Prefecture, ordered him into the city to summon and persuade Han Jian; Jian indeed came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder besieged Hua and sent Maye into the city to parley with Han Jian, who promptly surrendered.

sentences.zh: 及大軍在岐下，遣奏事於昭宗，再入復出。

translations.literal: When the great army was below Qi, he was sent to report to Zhaozong, entering twice and coming out again.
translations.idiomatic: While the army camped at Qi's walls he carried dispatches to Zhaozong, going in twice and returning each time.

sentences.zh: 又使於金州，說其帥馮行襲，俾堅攀附。

translations.literal: Again he was sent to Jin Prefecture to persuade its commander Feng Xingxi to hold fast to attachment.
translations.idiomatic: He was also sent to Jinzhou to bind Feng Xingxi firmly to the Founder's cause.

sentences.zh: 後曆宣武、天平等軍從事。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as staff officer of the Xuanyi and Tianping armies.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served on the staffs of the Xuanyi and Tianping commands.

sentences.zh: 開平元年，拜右武衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Kaiping year 1, he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiping he was made General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 三年，使於兩浙。

translations.literal: Year 3, he was envoy to the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: In his third year of office he was sent as envoy to the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 時淮路不通，乘駔者迂回萬里，陸行則出荊、襄、潭、桂入嶺，自番禺泛海至閩中，達於杭、越。

translations.literal: At that time the Huai route was not open; those who rode relay horses went round about ten thousand li; by land they went out through Jing, Xiang, Tan, Gui into the passes, from Panyu sailed the sea to Min, and reached Hang and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: With the Huai route cut, couriers wound ten thousand li overland—through Jing, Xiang, Tan, and Gui into the ranges, then by sea from Panyu into Fujian until they reached Hang and Yue.

sentences.zh: 復命則備舟楫，出東海，至於登、萊。

translations.literal: On return they prepared boats, went out the Eastern Sea, and reached Deng and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: The return passage meant fitting out ships, crossing the Eastern Sea, and making land at Deng and Lai.

sentences.zh: 而揚州諸步多賊船，過者不敢循岸，必高帆遠引海中，謂之「入陽」，以故多損敗。

translations.literal: But Yangzhou's posts had many bandit ships; passers did not dare hug the shore, but must raise sails and draw far off into the sea, called "Entering the Sun," and for this reason many were lost or wrecked.
translations.idiomatic: Pirate fleets held the Yangzhou coast, so travelers dared not hug the shore but put out to open sea—"entering the sun"—and many ships were lost that way.

sentences.zh: 鄴在海逾年，漂至躭羅國，一行俱溺。

translations.literal: Maye on the sea more than a year drifted to the Silla country; his whole party drowned together.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year at sea carried Maye to Silla, where his whole escort perished.

sentences.zh: 後詔贈司徒。

translations.literal: Later an edict posthumously gave him Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously named Grand Preceptor by edict.

sentences.zh: 劉捍，開封人。

translations.literal: Liu Han, a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Han came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父行仙，宣武軍大將。

translations.literal: His father Xingxian was a great general of the Xuanyi army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xingxian was a senior general of the Xuanyi army.

sentences.zh: 捍少為牙職，太祖初鎮夷門，以捍聰敏，擢副典客。

translations.literal: Han in youth was a yamen staffer; when the Founder first held Yimen he because Han was clever promoted him deputy master of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Han served in the yamen staff; when the Founder first took Bian he made the quick-witted Han his deputy master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 唐中和四年夏，太祖以朱珍為淄州刺史，令收兵於淄、青間，命捍監其兵，路逢大敵，皆破之。

translations.literal: Summer, Tang Zhonghe year 4, the Founder made Zhu Zhen prefect of Zi and ordered him to gather troops between Zi and Qing; he ordered Han to supervise his troops; on the road they met great enemies and all were broken.
translations.idiomatic: Summer of Zhonghe 4, the Founder sent Zhu Zhen to gather troops between Zi and Qing with Han overseeing his force; every major foe they met was defeated.

sentences.zh: 入博昌，獲精兵三萬以歸。

translations.literal: Entering Bochang, he obtained elite troops thirty thousand and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Bochang they took thirty thousand picked troops back with them.

sentences.zh: 四月，合大軍敗蔡賊秦宗賢數萬眾於汴西。

translations.literal: Fourth month, joining the great army he defeated the Cai bandit Qin Zongxian's host of tens of thousands west of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the combined army routed tens of thousands of Qin Zongxian's Cai rebels west of Bian.

sentences.zh: 文德元年十一月，蔡將申叢折宗權足，納款於太祖，使捍奏其事，加兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Wende year 1, eleventh month, the Cai general Shen Cong broke Zongquan's foot, submitted to the Founder; he had Han report the affair and added him concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Wende 1 the Cai general Shen Cong broke Zongquan's foot and surrendered; Han carried word of it to the Founder and received concurrent rank as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 光化三年六月，太祖北伐鎮、定，至常山，而王钅容危懾，送款於太祖，命捍入壁門傳諭。

translations.literal: Guanghua year 3, sixth month, the Founder north campaigned against Zhen and Ding, reaching Changshan; Wang Rong in peril and fear sent submission to the Founder, and ordered Han to enter the barbican gate to proclaim the message.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guanghua 3 the Founder marched north against Zhen and Ding; at Changshan a terrified Wang Rong submitted, and the Founder sent Han through the barbican to announce terms.

sentences.zh: 時兩軍未整，守門者戈戟千匝，捍馳騎而入，竟達其命。

translations.literal: At that time the two armies were not yet arrayed; gate guards with spears and halberds ringed a thousandfold; Han galloped in on horseback and at last delivered his charge.
translations.idiomatic: While both armies were still unprepared, spears ringed the gate a thousand deep; Han rode straight through and carried out his orders.

sentences.zh: 又移師以攻中山，至懷德驛，大破定人五萬眾，王處直乞降，捍復單馬入州，安撫而回。

translations.literal: Again he moved troops to attack Zhongshan; reaching Huaidi post, he greatly defeated Ding's fifty thousand; Wang Chuzhi begged surrender; Han again entered the prefecture alone on horseback, pacified, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Zhongshan next; at Huaidi post fifty thousand men of Ding were shattered; Wang Chuzhi sued for peace; Han rode in alone again to calm the city and came back.

sentences.zh: 太祖迎昭宗於岐下，以捍為親軍指揮。

translations.literal: The Founder welcomed Zhaozong below Qi and made Han commander of the personal army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder welcomed Zhaozong at Qi's walls, he made Han commander of his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 天復三年正月，宋文通令客將郭啟奇使於太祖，命捍復命。

translations.literal: Tianfu year 3, first month, Song Wentong ordered the guest-officer Guo Qiqi as envoy to the Founder and ordered Han to answer the mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianfu 3, Song Wentong sent his guest-officer Guo Qiqi to the Founder with Han as the envoy to reply.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聞其至，即召見，詢東兵之事，仍以錦服、銀鞍勒馬賜之。

translations.literal: Zhaozong hearing he had arrived at once summoned him, asked about eastern army affairs, and also bestowed brocade robes and a silver-saddled bridled horse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong summoned him at once, questioned him on the eastern armies, and gave him brocade robes and a horse with silver saddle and bridle.

sentences.zh: 翌日，授光祿大夫、檢校司空、登州刺史。

translations.literal: The next day he was granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Sikong, and made prefect of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he received Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Sikong, and the prefecture of Deng.

sentences.zh: 昭宗還京，改常州刺史，賜號迎鑾毅勇功臣。

translations.literal: Zhaozong returned to the capital, changed him to Chang prefect and gave the title Meritous Minister Courageously Welcoming the Imperial Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong returned to the capital Han became prefect of Chang and received the title "Meritous Minister for Courageously Welcoming the Imperial Chariot."

sentences.zh: 四月，太祖伐王師範於青州，改左右長直都指揮使。

translations.literal: Fourth month, the Founder campaigned against Wang Shifan at Qingzhou and changed him to commander of the left and right Long-Straight commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, as the Founder attacked Wang Shifan at Qingzhou, Han was made commander of the left and right Long-Straight guards.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年正月，授宋州刺史。

translations.literal: Tianyou year 3, first month, he was granted Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianyou 3 he was made prefect of Song.

sentences.zh: 四月，加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Fourth month, added acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he received acting rank as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，授左龍虎統軍兼元從新軍馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: The Founder received the abdication and appointed him commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Guard and concurrently chief military adjutant of the original-following new army, horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne he made Han commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Guard and chief adjutant of his personal new army, horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 及上黨纏兵，太祖親往巡撫，以捍為御營使。

translations.literal: When Shangdang tangled troops, the Founder in person went to oversee; he made Han imperial-camp commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When war tangled at Shangdang the Founder went in person and made Han commissioner of the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 大軍次昂車，斥候來告蕃戎逼澤州，命捍以兵千人赴之，並軍遂遁，車駕還京，授捍侍衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: The great army halted at Angche; scouts came reporting barbarians pressing Ze Prefecture; he ordered Han with a thousand troops to go; the combined armies thereupon fled; the imperial carriage returned to the capital and Han was granted commander of the personal guard of the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Angche; scouts reported barbarians pressing Ze; the Founder sent Han with a thousand men and the enemy fled; when the emperor returned to the capital Han was made commander of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 晉人侵晉州，從幸陝回，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: Jin men invaded Jin Prefecture; following the imperial progress to Shan and back, he was added acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin struck Jinzhou and Han followed the court to Shan and back, he received acting rank as Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 及從駕幸河中，詔追王重師赴行在，以捍為雍州節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: When he followed the carriage to Hezhong, an edict recalled Wang Chongshi to the traveling court and made Han regent military commissioner and surveillance commissioner of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Hezhong, Wang Chongshi was recalled and Han was made acting military and surveillance commissioner of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 才逾月，劉知俊據同州反，潛使人以厚利啖將校，遂為部下所執，送於知俊。

translations.literal: Barely past a month, Liu Zhijun held Tong Prefecture and rebelled, secretly sent men with thick profit to entice commanders; Han was thereupon seized by subordinates and sent to Zhijun.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month later Liu Zhijun rebelled at Tongzhou and secretly bribed Han's officers; they seized him and handed him to Zhijun.

sentences.zh: 知俊縶捍歸於鳳翔，為李茂貞所害。

translations.literal: Zhijun bound Han and returned to Fengxiang; he was harmed by Li Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun sent Han bound to Fengxiang, where Li Maozhen put him to death.

sentences.zh: 開平四年，贈太傅。

translations.literal: Kaiping year 4, gifted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 4 he was posthumously named Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，又贈太尉。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, again gifted Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor ascended he was posthumously named Grand Commandant as well.

sentences.zh: 捍便習賓讚，善於將迎，自司賓局及征討四出，必預其間。

translations.literal: Han was skilled at guest rites and acclamation, good at receiving and escorting; from the Bureau of Guest Rites and on campaigns in four directions he was always in their midst.
translations.idiomatic: Han mastered guest rites and welcome ceremony; from the Bureau of Guest Rites to every campaign abroad he was always in the thick of it.

sentences.zh: 雖無決戰爭鋒之績，而承命奔走，數揚命令，勤幹涖職，以至崇顯焉。

translations.literal: Though he had no achievement of decisive battle and contending edge, yet receiving orders he ran and hastened, repeatedly proclaimed commands, diligently carried office—and so reached eminent display.
translations.idiomatic: He won no great battle, yet by racing on every order, bearing the Founder's word again and again, and tireless service he rose to the highest honors.

sentences.zh: 王敬蕘，潁州汝陰人，世為郡武吏。

translations.literal: Wang Jinrao, a man of Ruyin in Ying Prefecture, for generations were the prefecture's military clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinrao of Ruyin in Yingzhou came from a line of county military officers.

sentences.zh: 唐乾符初，敬蕘為本州都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Early Tang Qianfu, Jinrao was the prefecture's commander knowing horse and troops.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianfu he became the prefecture's commander of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 中和初，寇難益熾，郡守庸怯，不能自固，敬蕘遂代之監郡，俄真拜刺史，加檢校右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Early Zhonghe, bandit calamity burned hotter; the prefect was mediocre and timid and could not secure himself; Jinrao thereupon replaced him supervising the prefecture, soon truly appointed prefect, added acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhonghe, as raids grew fiercer and the timid prefect could not hold the city, Jinrao took charge of the circuit, was soon confirmed as prefect, and given acting rank as Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時州境荒饉，大寇繼至，黃巢數十萬眾寨於州南，敬蕘極力抗禦，逾旬而退。

translations.literal: At that time the prefecture's borders were waste and famine; great bandits came in succession; Huang Chao's hundreds of thousands camped south of the prefecture; Jinrao strove with all strength to resist; after ten days and more they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Famine stalked the circuit while great armies came one after another; hundreds of thousands of Huang Chao's men camped south of the city, and Jinrao fought them off until they withdrew after more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 俄又宗權之眾，淩暴益甚，合圍攻壁，皆力屈而去。

translations.literal: Soon again Zongquan's hosts, outrage growing worse, joined siege and stormed walls; all strained their strength and left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zongquan's forces came with still worse violence, besieged the walls, and withdrew only when their strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊復遣將刁君務以萬眾來逼，敬蕘列陣當之，身先馳突，殺敵甚多，由是竟全郡壘，遠近歸附。

translations.literal: The Cai bandits again sent the general Diao Junwu with ten thousand hosts to press; Jinrao arrayed ranks to meet them, himself first galloping in charge, killed enemies very many; thereby he at last preserved the whole prefecture's fortresses; near and far submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Cai rebels sent Diao Junwu with ten thousand men; Jinrao formed his line, led the charge himself, and killed a great many; the walls held, and men near and far came to his banner.

sentences.zh: 及淮人不恭，太祖屢以軍南渡，路由州境，敬蕘悉心供億，太祖甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When Huainan men were not respectful, the Founder repeatedly with armies crossed south, the route passing through his prefectural borders; Jinrao with whole heart supplied provisions; the Founder greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Each time the Founder crossed the Huai with an army and passed through Ying, Jinrao supplied his needs without stint, and the Founder took great notice.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，署為沿淮上下都指揮使。

translations.literal: Qianning year 2, he was appointed commander of all posts along the Huai above and below.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 2 he was named commander of all forces along the upper and lower Huai.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，龐師古敗於清口，敗軍逃歸者甚眾，路出於潁。

translations.literal: Winter, year 4, Pang Shigu was defeated at Qingkou; defeated armies fleeing back were very many; the road went out through Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Winter of year 4, after Pang Shigu's defeat at Qingkou, shattered troops poured homeward through Ying.

sentences.zh: 時雨雪連旬，軍士凍餒，敬蕘自淮燎薪，相屬於道，郡中設糜糗餅餌以待之，全活者甚眾，由是表知武寧軍節度、徐宿觀察留後。

translations.literal: At that time rain and snow continued ten days; soldiers froze and starved; Jinrao from the Huai sent fire and fuel, one after another on the road; in the prefecture he set out gruel, dry provisions, and cakes to wait for them; very many were wholly kept alive; thereby memorialized as acting Wuning army military commissioner and Xuzhou-Suzhou surveillance regent.
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell ten days running; the troops were freezing and starving; Jinrao sent fuel from the Huai along the road and set out gruel and cakes in the city; many lived because of it, and he was memorialized acting commissioner of Wuning and regent of Xuzhou and Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 數月，真拜武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: Several months, truly appointed Wuning army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he was confirmed full military commissioner of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 天復二年，入為右龍武統軍。

translations.literal: Tianfu year 2, entered [the capital] as commander of the Right Dragon-Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 2 he was called to the capital as commander of the Right Dragon-Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，轉左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Tianyou year 3, transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 3 he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 開平元年八月，以疾致仕，尋卒於其第。

translations.literal: Kaiping year 1, eighth month, on illness he retired from office; soon after he died at his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Kaiping 1 he retired for illness and soon died at home.

sentences.zh: 敬蕘魁傑沈勇，多力善戰，所用槍矢，皆以純鐵鍛就，槍重三十餘斤，摧鋒突陣，率以此勝。

translations.literal: Jinrao was a towering hero, deep and brave, much strength and good at battle; the spears and arrows he used were all forged of pure iron; the spear weighed more than thirty jin; crushing the vanguard and piercing arrays, he generally won by this.
translations.idiomatic: Jinrao was a towering man, deep and brave; his spears and arrows were forged from solid iron, his spear alone weighed more than thirty pounds, and he broke enemy lines by sheer weight of steel.

sentences.zh: 雖非太祖舊臣，而遠輸懇款，保境合兵，以輔興王之運，有足稱者。

translations.literal: Though not an old minister of the Founder, yet from afar he conveyed earnest pledge, preserved borders and united troops, to assist the fortune of the rising king—there is enough to praise.
translations.idiomatic: He was no veteran of the Founder's camp, yet from afar he offered loyal service, held his territory, and marshaled troops to help the new dynasty—grounds enough for praise.

sentences.zh: 高劭，字子將，淮南節度使駢之從子也。

translations.literal: Gao Shao, styled Zijiang, was the younger cousin of Huainan military commissioner Gao Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shao, who styled himself Zijiang, was a cousin of the Huainan commissioner Gao Pian.

sentences.zh: 父泰，黔中觀察使。

translations.literal: His father Tai was Qianzhong surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tai had been surveillance commissioner of Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 唐僖宗避敵在蜀，駢鎮淮南為都統，兼諸道鹽鐵使，兵賦在己，朝廷優假之，以故劭幸而早官，年十四遙領華州刺史。

translations.literal: Tang Emperor Xizong avoided the enemy in Shu; Pian held Huainan as supreme commander and concurrently salt and iron commissioner for all circuits, troops and levies in his own hands—the court treated him generously; thus Shao by fortune received early office, at age fourteen distantly holding Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While Xizong sheltered in Shu, Pian ruled Huainan as supreme commander and salt-and-iron commissioner with troops and taxes in his fist; the court indulged him, and Shao at fourteen was given distant command as prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 光啟中，以駢命遏晉公王鐸於鄭。

translations.literal: Mid Guangqi, on Pian's order he blocked the Duke of Jin Wang Duo at Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through Guangqi he blocked Wang Duo, Duke of Jin, at Zheng on Pian's order.

sentences.zh: 俄而州陷於蔡，劭為賊所得，使人守之，戒四門曰：「無出高大夫。

translations.literal: Soon the prefecture fell to Cai; Shao was taken by bandits; they sent men to guard him and warned the four gates: "Do not let High Excellency out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Cai rebels took the city; they seized Shao and posted guards with orders at every gate: "Let no one let Lord Gao out.

sentences.zh: 」劭伺守者稍惰，佯為乞食者，過危垣，取殍者衣，坌身易服，得他兒抱之行，出東郊門。

translations.literal: " Shao watched until guards slackened slightly, pretended to be a beggar-for-food, passed a perilous wall, took a corpse's clothes, covered his body and changed dress, got another child to carry and walked, exiting the eastern suburb gate.
translations.idiomatic: " When the guards slackened he played a beggar, crept past a broken wall, dressed in a dead man's rags, took up another child as if his own, and walked out the eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 人以為丐者，不之止。

translations.literal: People took him for a beggar and did not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Passers took him for a beggar and let him go.

sentences.zh: 及稍遠，棄所抱兒，疾趨至中牟，遂達於汴。

translations.literal: When somewhat far, he abandoned the child he carried, hastened swiftly to Zhongmu, and at last reached Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was clear of the city he abandoned the child, ran to Zhongmu, and reached Bian.

sentences.zh: 太祖以客禮遇之，尋表為亳州團練副使，知州事。

translations.literal: The Founder treated him with guest rites; soon memorialized him as Bozhou regimental vice-commissioner and acting prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder received him as an honored guest and soon made him vice-regimental commissioner at Bozhou with charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又數年，辟為宣武軍節度判官，在幕下頗以氣直自許。

translations.literal: Again several years, summoned as Xuanyi army military commissioner adjutant; in the staff he quite took straight spirit as his boast.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he joined the Xuanyi staff as chief adjutant and prided himself on blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 後監鄭州事，復權知徐州留後。

translations.literal: Later he supervised Zheng Prefecture affairs and again held acting authority as Xuzhou regent.
translations.idiomatic: He later oversaw Zhengzhou and served acting regent at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗之鳳翔，太祖迎奉未出，劭有疑謀，遂令赴華州，詣丞相府以議其事；

translations.literal: Tang Emperor Zhaozong went to Fengxiang; the Founder had not yet gone out to welcome him; Shao had doubtful schemes; he was then ordered to go to Hua Prefecture, to approach the chief minister's office to deliberate the affair;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong fled to Fengxiang and the Founder had not yet marched to receive him, Shao's plotting aroused suspicion; he was sent to Hua to consult the chief minister's office—

sentences.zh: 行至高陵，為盜所害。

translations.literal: traveling, reaching Gaoling, he was harmed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: on the road at Gaoling bandits killed him.

sentences.zh: 馬嗣勳，濠州鍾離縣人，世為軍吏。

translations.literal: Ma Sixun, a man of Zhongli county in Hao Prefecture, for generations military clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sixun of Zhongli in Haozhou came from a family of army officers.

sentences.zh: 嗣勳有口辯，習武藝，初為州客將。

translations.literal: Sixun had mouth and debate, practised martial arts; at first he was the prefecture's guest-officer.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun was eloquent and trained in arms; he began as the prefecture's guest-officer.

sentences.zh: 唐景福元年三月，太祖以壽州刺史江儒反下蔡鎮使，李立率兵攻濠梁，刺史張遂俾嗣勳持州印籍戶口以歸於太祖。

translations.literal: Tang Jingfu year 1, third month, the Founder because Shou prefect Jiang Ru rebelled [at] Xia'ai garrison commander Li Li led troops attacking Hao and Liang; prefect Zhang Sui had Sixun hold the prefectural seal and register households to return submission to the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Jingfu 1, when Shou prefect Jiang Ru rebelled at Xia'ai, Li Li attacked Hao and Liang; prefect Zhang Sui sent Sixun with the seal and household registers to submit to the Founder.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年三月，楊行密復攻濠州，張遂遣嗣勳求援於太祖。

translations.literal: Qianning year 2, third month, Yang Xingmi again attacked Hao Prefecture; Zhang Sui sent Sixun to beg aid from the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Qianning 2, when Yang Xingmi attacked Haozhou again, Zhang Sui sent Sixun to plead for help.

sentences.zh: 俄而郡陷，嗣勳無所歸，即署為元從押牙、副典客，頗稱任使。

translations.literal: Soon the prefecture fell; Sixun had nowhere to return; he was at once appointed original-following yamen adjutant and deputy master of ceremonies, quite fit for employment and missions.
translations.idiomatic: When the city soon fell Sixun had nowhere to go; the Founder made him yamen adjutant of his personal following and deputy master of ceremonies, and found him thoroughly reliable.

sentences.zh: 光化元年三月，太祖令往光州說刺史劉存背淮賊以向國，又從李彥威復黃州及武昌縣，獲刺史瞿章。

translations.literal: Guanghua 1 third month, the Founder sent him to Guang prefecture to persuade Prefect Liu Cun to turn from Huai bandits toward the state; he also followed Li Yanwei to recover Huang prefecture and Wuchang county and captured Prefect Qu Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Guanghua 1 the Founder sent him to Guangzhou to urge Liu Cun to abandon the Huai rebels for the throne; he then joined Li Yanwei in retaking Huangzhou and Wuchang county and took Prefect Qu Zhang captive.

sentences.zh: 俄復使光州，持幣馬以賜劉存。

translations.literal: Soon he was again sent to Guang prefecture, bearing silks and horses to bestow on Liu Cun.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dispatched to Guangzhou again with gifts of silk and horses for Liu Cun.

sentences.zh: 會淮賊急攻光州，存與嗣勳率兵大戰，敗而走之。

translations.literal: When Huai bandits pressed Guang prefecture in force, Cun and Sixun led troops in great battle and defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai rebels stormed Guangzhou, Liu Cun and Sixun gave battle and routed them.

sentences.zh: 又遣使於蜀，及歸，得其助軍貲實甚多。

translations.literal: He also was sent as envoy to Shu; on return he obtained very much military aid in goods and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He later went as envoy to Shu and on his return brought back abundant military stores.

sentences.zh: 天復中，太祖迎昭宗於岐下，軍至華之西，使嗣勳入見，韓建即時同出迎謁。

translations.literal: In Tianfu, when the Founder welcomed Zhaozong at Qixia and the army reached west of Hua, he sent Sixun in to see him; Han Jian at once came out together to welcome and pay court.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu, as the Founder brought Zhaozong from Qixia and halted west of Hua, he sent Sixun in to audience; Han Jian came out at once to greet them together.

sentences.zh: 及羅紹威將殺牙軍，遣使告於太祖，求為外援。

translations.literal: When Luo Shaowei was about to kill the guard army, he sent envoys to inform the Founder and beg for outside aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Shaowei planned to destroy the guard corps, he asked the Founder for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 時安陽公主初卒於魏，太祖乃遺嗣勳率長直官千人，實兵仗於橐中，肩舁以入於魏，聲言來致祭會葬，牙軍不之覺。

translations.literal: At the time Princess Anyang had just died in Wei; the Founder then sent Sixun leading a thousand long-guard officers, with weapons packed in chests and borne on shoulders into Wei, declaring they came to offer sacrifice at the funeral—the guard army did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anyang had just died at Wei; the Founder sent Sixun with a thousand hand-picked men, weapons hidden in coffers carried on poles into the city under cover of funeral rites, and the guard army never suspected.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年正月十六日夜，嗣勳與紹威親軍同攻牙軍，至曙，盡殪之。

translations.literal: Tianyou 3 first month, night of the sixteenth, Sixun with Shaowei's personal troops together attacked the guard army; by dawn they were all annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the sixteenth of the first month of Tianyou 3, Sixun and Shaowei's own troops struck the guard corps and wiped them out by dawn.

sentences.zh: 嗣勳重傷，旬日而卒。

translations.literal: Sixun was gravely wounded and died within ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun was badly wounded and died ten days later.

sentences.zh: 開平中，累贈太保。

translations.literal: In Kaiping he was repeatedly posthumously promoted to Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiping he was posthumously raised to Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 張存敬，譙郡人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Cunjing was a man of Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cunjin came from Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 性剛直，有膽勇，臨危無所畏憚。

translations.literal: By nature upright and firm, with courage and daring, in facing peril he had no fear or dread.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, bold, and utterly fearless in danger, he never flinched.

sentences.zh: 唐中和中，從太祖赴汴，以其折節，頗見親昵，首為右騎都將。

translations.literal: In Tang Zhonghe he followed the Founder to Bian; because of his self-restraint he was quite treated with intimacy, and first became Right Cavalry commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhonghe of Tang he followed the Founder to Bian; his discipline won favor, and he became the first Right Cavalry commander.

sentences.zh: 從討巢、蔡，凡曆百戰，多於危蹙之間，顯有奇略，由是頻立殊效。

translations.literal: Following campaigns against Chao and Cai, in all he passed through a hundred battles; many times in moments of dire straits he showed strange strategy, and thereby repeatedly established extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the wars on Chao and Cai he fought a hundred engagements and, again and again in tight corners, showed brilliant tactics that won him repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 光啟中，李罕之會晉軍圍張宗奭於盟津，太祖遣丁會、葛從周、存敬同往馳救。

translations.literal: In Guangqi, Li Hanzhi joined Jin troops in besieging Zhang Zongshi at Meng Ford; the Founder sent Ding Hui, Ge Congzhou, and Cunjing together to gallop to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangqi, Li Hanzhi and the Jin besieged Zhang Zongshi at Mengjin; the Founder sent Ding Hui, Ge Congzhou, and Cunjin to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 存敬引騎軍先犯敵將，諸軍翼之，敵騎大敗，乃解河橋之圍。

translations.literal: Cunjing led cavalry first to strike the enemy commander; the armies flanked him; enemy horsemen were greatly defeated, and thus the siege at He Bridge was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjin led the cavalry against the enemy commander while the rest flanked; the Jin horse were routed and the siege of He Bridge was broken.

sentences.zh: 大順二年，為諸軍都虞候，佐霍存董大軍收宿州，以功奏加檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Datong 2 he became overall army inspector, assisted Huo Cun in directing the great army to recover Suzhou, and for merit was memorialized Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 2 he was made army inspector, helped Huo Cun retake Suzhou, and was memorialized Acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 太祖東征徐、兗，存敬屢有俘斬之功。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned east against Xu and Yan, Cunjing repeatedly had merit in captures and beheadings.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern campaigns against Xu and Yan, Cunjin took many prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 凡受指顧，皆與機會，矢石所及，必以身先，太祖屢加優異，以為行營都指揮使、檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: Whenever he received orders he always seized the moment; wherever arrows and stones reached he must take the lead; the Founder repeatedly showed him special favor and made him field army overall commander and Acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He seized every chance in battle and always led where stones and arrows fell; the Founder favored him and made him field commander and Acting Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 乾寧三年，充武寧軍留後，行潁州刺史。

translations.literal: Qianning 3 he served as Wuning army acting commissioner, acting Yingzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 3 he was acting Wuning commissioner and prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 光化二年夏四月，幽、滄侵淩魏郡，復以存敬為都指揮使。

translations.literal: Guanghua 2 summer fourth month, You and Cang harassed and encroached on Wei commandery; Cunjing was again made overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Guanghua 2, when You and Cang raided Wei, Cunjin was again made overall commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，大舉，與葛從周連統諸軍攻浮陽，樹數十柵，圍劉守文累月。

translations.literal: Year 3, on a great campaign, with Ge Congzhou jointly commanded the armies attacking Fuyang, erected several tens of stockades, and besieged Liu Shouwen for many months.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he joined Ge Congzhou in a major siege of Fuyang, building dozens of camps around Liu Shouwen for months.

sentences.zh: 時幽州劉仁恭舉兵來援，存敬潛軍擊之於乾寧軍南老鴉堤。

translations.literal: At the time Youzhou's Liu Rengong raised troops to aid; Cunjing secretly moved troops and struck him at Old Crow Embankment south of Qianning army.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Rengong of Youzhou marched to relieve the city, Cunjin ambushed him at Old Crow Embankment south of Qianning.

sentences.zh: 是日，燕人大敗，斬首五萬級，生擒馬慎交已下一百餘人，獲馬萬餘蹄。

translations.literal: That day the Yan men were greatly defeated; heads cut numbered fifty thousand; alive captured Ma Shenjiao and over a hundred below him; horses obtained over ten thousand hooves.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Yan army was shattered: fifty thousand heads, more than a hundred captives led by Ma Shenjiao, and over ten thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 其年秋九月，引軍收鎮州，存敬勒眾涉滹沲河，師人鼓行而進，逢鎮之遊兵數千，因逐之，直入鎮之壅門，收鞍馬牛駝萬計。

translations.literal: That year autumn ninth month, he led the army to take Zhen prefecture; Cunjing drove the masses across the Hutuo River; the army beat drums and advanced; met several thousand of Zhen's roaming troops; thereupon pursued them, straight into Zhen's barrier gate, and collected saddles, horses, cattle, and camels by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he marched on Zhenzhou; Cunjin crossed the Hutuo at the drum, routed several thousand scouts, chased them through the barrier gate, and seized tens of thousands of animals.

sentences.zh: 翌日，鎮人納質而旋。

translations.literal: The next day the Zhen men offered hostages and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhenzhou submitted hostages and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋為宋州刺史，逾年，甚有能政。

translations.literal: Soon he became Song prefect; after more than a year he was very able in government.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became prefect of Songzhou and governed ably for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 復擁眾伐薊門，數旬間連下瀛、莫、祁、景四州，擒俘不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Again he led masses to campaign against Ji Gate; within several tens of days in succession he took Ying, Mo, Qi, and Jing four prefectures; prisoners captured could not be fully counted.
translations.idiomatic: He again marched on Ji Gate and within weeks took Ying, Mo, Qi, and Jing, with captives beyond count.

sentences.zh: 自懷德驛與中山兵接戰，枕屍數十里，中山開壁請降。

translations.literal: From Huaide post he joined battle with Zhongshan troops; corpses pillowed for several tens of li; Zhongshan opened the walls and begged surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Huaide post he fought the Zhongshan army until the dead lay for miles; Zhongshan opened the walls and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 天復元年春，太祖以河中節度使王珂與太原結親，憑恃驕恣，命存敬統大軍討之。

translations.literal: Tianfu 1 spring, the Founder because Hezhong military commissioner Wang Ke had allied with Taiyuan and relied on arrogance and license ordered Cunjing to command the great army to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Tianfu 1 the Founder, angered that Wang Ke of Hezhong had married into Taiyuan and grown insolent, sent Cunjin with a great army against him.

sentences.zh: 即日收絳州，擒刺史陶建釗，降晉州刺史張漢瑜，二郡平。

translations.literal: That very day he took Jiang prefecture, captured Prefect Tao Jianzhao, and Jiang prefecture's Zhang Hanyu submitted; the two commanderies were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The same day he took Jiangzhou, seized Tao Jianzhao, and won Zhang Hanyu of Jinzhou—both districts were pacified.

sentences.zh: 進圍河中，王珂請降。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Hezhong, Wang Ke begged surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Hezhong until Wang Ke surrendered.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，乃以存敬為護國軍留後。

translations.literal: The Founder praised this and thereupon made Cunjing Huguo army acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was pleased and made Cunjin acting commissioner of Huguo.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校司空，尋移宋州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, Acting Minister of Works; soon moved to Song prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Acting Minister of Works, then transferred to Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 將之任所，寢疾，逾旬卒於河中。

translations.literal: About to go to his post of office, he took to bed with illness; after more than ten days he died at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to take up Songzhou he fell ill and died at Hezhong within a fortnight.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，痛惜移晷。

translations.literal: When the Founder heard it he grieved and regretted for a watch.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder mourned him for hours on hearing the news.

sentences.zh: 開平初，追贈太保。

translations.literal: At Kaiping's opening, posthumously enfeoffed Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Kaiping he was posthumously made Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 乾化三年，又追贈太傅。

translations.literal: Qianhua 3, again posthumously enfeoffed Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianhua 3 he was posthumously raised to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 子仁願，晉天福中，仕至大理。

translations.literal: His son Renyuan, in Jin Tianfu, reached office as chief judge of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renyuan rose under Later Jin to chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 寇彥卿，字俊臣，大梁人也。

translations.literal: Kou Yanqing, style Junchen, was a man of Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Yanqing, styled Junchen, came from Daliang.

sentences.zh: 祖琯，父裔，皆宣武軍牙校。

translations.literal: Grandfather Guan and father Yi were both Xuanwu army guard officers.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guan and father Yi had both been guard officers of the Xuanwu army.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮汴，以彥卿將家子，擢在左右。

translations.literal: When the Founder held Bian he, because Yanqing was a general's son, promoted him to his side.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder governed Bian he kept Yanqing, a general's son, at his side.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，選為通讚官。

translations.literal: At weak cap he was chosen as communications officer.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was made a protocol officer.

sentences.zh: 太祖為元帥，補元帥府押牙，充四鎮通讚官行首兼右長直都指揮使，累奏授檢校司徒，領洺州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Founder was grand marshal he supplemented him as the marshal's headquarters guard officer, served as head of the four commands communications officers and concurrently Right Long Direct overall commander, and repeatedly memorialized to appoint Acting Minister of Works and grant Ming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As grand marshal the Founder made him headquarters guard officer, chief protocol officer of the four commands and Right Long Direct commander, and had him memorialized Acting Minister of Works and prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 羅紹威將殺牙軍，遣使告於太祖，太祖命彥卿使於魏，密與紹威謀之。

translations.literal: When Luo Shaowei was about to kill the guard army he sent envoys to inform the Founder; the Founder ordered Yanqing as envoy to Wei to plot secretly with Shaowei.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Shaowei moved against the guard corps he asked the Founder for help; the Founder sent Yanqing to Wei to conspire with him.

sentences.zh: 竟成其事，彥卿之力也。

translations.literal: In the end the affair succeeded—Yanqing's strength.
translations.idiomatic: The plot succeeded largely through Yanqing's efforts.

sentences.zh: 彥卿身長八尺，隆準方面，語音如鍾。

translations.literal: Yanqing was eight feet in height, with high nose and square face; his voice was like a bell.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing stood eight feet tall, with a high nose and square face, and a voice like a bell.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，好書史，復善伺太祖之旨，凡所作為，動皆云合。

translations.literal: Skilled in mounted archery, fond of books and histories, and again skilled at reading the Founder's intent—whatever he did always matched like clouds joining.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at riding and archery, loved history, and read the Founder's mind so well that his every act seemed foreordained.

sentences.zh: 太祖每言曰：「敬翔、劉捏、寇彥卿，蓋為我而生。

translations.literal: The Founder often said: "Jing Xiang, Liu Han, and Kou Yanqing were surely born for me.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder would say: "Jing Xiang, Liu Han, and Kou Yanqing might as well have been made for me.

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: 」Thus he was valued to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Such was the esteem in which he held them.

sentences.zh: 太祖有所乘烏馬，號「一丈烏」，嘗以賜彥卿。

translations.literal: The Founder had a black horse he rode called "One Zhang Crow"; he once bestowed it on Yanqing.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder once gave him his black charger, the "Ten-foot Crow."

sentences.zh: 天復中，太祖迎昭宗於鳳翔，累與岐軍對陣。

translations.literal: In Tianfu, when the Founder welcomed Zhaozong at Fengxiang, he repeatedly faced Qi troops in array.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu, as the Founder brought Zhaozong from Fengxiang, he fought the Qi army again and again.

sentences.zh: 時彥卿為諸道馬步軍都排陣使。

translations.literal: At the time Yanqing was overall array marshal of all circuits horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing then served as overall battle-line marshal for the allied forces.

sentences.zh: 嘗躬擐甲胄，乘其所賜烏馬，馳騁於陣前，太祖目之曰：「真神王也！

translations.literal: He once personally donned armor and helmet, rode the black horse bestowed on him, and galloped before the lines; the Founder eyed him and said: "Truly a spirit king!
translations.idiomatic: Once, armored and mounted on his gifted black horse, he charged before the ranks; the Founder watched and cried, "A true war god!

sentences.zh: 」昭宗還京，賜迎鑾毅勇功臣，改邢州刺史，尋遷亳州團練使。

translations.literal: 」When Zhaozong returned to the capital he was granted the title Welcome-the-Chariot Bold and Brave Merit Subject, changed to Xing prefect, and soon moved to Bozhou regimental commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: 」 After Zhaozong returned to the capital he received the merit title Welcome-the-Chariot Bold and Brave, became prefect of Xingzhou, and soon regimental commissioner of Bozhou.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Kou Yanqing's Huainan command:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Kou Yanqing's Huainan command:

sentences.zh: （案《通鑒》：開平二年，帝從吳越王錢鏐之請，以亳州團練使寇彥卿為東南面行營都指揮使，使擊淮南。

translations.literal: （Case note from the 《Comprehensive Mirror》: In Kaiping 2, the Emperor at King Qian Liu of Wuyue's request made Bozhou regimental commissioner Kou Yanqing southeast campaign overall commander to attack Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: In Kaiping 2, at Wuyue king Qian Liu's request the Emperor named Kou Yanqing of Bozhou overall commander of the southeast campaign against Huainan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，彥卿率眾一千襲霍丘，為土豪朱景所敗；

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Yanqing led a thousand men to raid Huoqiu and was defeated by local strongman Zhu Jing;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yanqing led a thousand men against Huoqiu and was beaten by the local chief Zhu Jing;

sentences.zh: 又攻廬、壽二州，皆不勝。

translations.literal: again attacked Lu and Shou two prefectures, both without victory.
translations.idiomatic: he then attacked Lu and Shou and failed in both.

sentences.zh: 淮南遣滁州刺史李儼拒之。

translations.literal: Huainan sent Chuzhou prefect Li Yi to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan sent Li Yi, prefect of Chuzhou, to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 《九國誌·朱景傳》：梁祖聞景名，命寇彥卿率勁騎三千襲霍丘，圖取景，且諭梁祖之意令降，景率其徒戰於丘墟林澤中，射死者無數，彥卿兵折力殫而去。）〉

translations.literal: The 《Chronicle of the Nine States · Biography of Zhu Jing》: The Liang Founder heard Jing's fame and ordered Kou Yanqing to lead three thousand crack horsemen to raid Huoqiu, intending to capture Jing, and also conveyed the Liang Founder's intent that he submit; Jing led his followers to fight in ruined mounds and forest marsh; those shot dead were countless; Yanqing's troops were broken and strength exhausted and departed.）〉
translations.idiomatic: The 《Nine States Chronicle · Biography of Zhu Jing》 says the Liang Founder sent Yanqing with three thousand elite cavalry to take Huoqiu and capture Jing, offering surrender terms; Jing fought him in scrub and marsh, killing many; Yanqing withdrew with his force spent.）〉

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，為華州節度使，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the mandate he became Hua prefecture military commissioner, added Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: At the Liang founding he became military commissioner of Huazhou with Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，入為左金吾衛大將軍，充街使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he entered as Left Golden Crow Guard grand general and served as street commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he entered court as grand general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and city street commissioner.

sentences.zh: 一日，過天津橋，有老人誤衝其趨道者，排之，落橋而斃，為御史府所彈，太祖不得已，責授左衛中郎將。

translations.literal: One day, crossing Tianjin Bridge, an old man by mistake rushed into his path of travel; he pushed him; he fell from the bridge and died; the censorate impeached him; the Founder had no choice and demoted him to Left Guard middle-rank general.
translations.idiomatic: Once on Tianjin Bridge an old man blundered into his path; Yanqing shoved him off the bridge to his death; the censors impeached him, and the Founder reluctantly demoted him to middle-rank general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 不數月，除相州防禦使，依前行營諸軍排陣使。

translations.literal: Within several months he was appointed Xiangzhou defense commissioner, retaining his former post as field army array marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was made defense commissioner of Xiangzhou while keeping his post as army array marshal.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授河陽節度使，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: Before long he was granted Heyang military commissioner, added Acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received Heyang as military commissioner with Acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 及太祖遇弑，彥卿追感舊恩，圖御容以奠之。

translations.literal: When the Founder met assassination, Yanqing recalled old favor and painted the imperial likeness to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founder was murdered, Yanqing painted his portrait and made offerings in memory of old kindness.

sentences.zh: 每因對客言及先朝舊事，即涕泗交流。

translations.literal: Whenever in facing guests he spoke of former-court old affairs, tears and mucus would stream together.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of the former court before guests he wept openly.

sentences.zh: 末帝嗣位，遙領興元節度使、東南面行營都招討使。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded, he held at a distance Xingyuan military commissioner and southeast campaign overall commander to suppress and recruit.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Last Emperor he held Xingyuan and the southeast suppression command in absentia.

sentences.zh: 以拒淮寇，尋改右金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: To resist Huai bandits, soon changed to Right Golden Crow Guard senior general.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting the Huai rebels, he was soon made senior general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞明初，授鄧州節度使。

translations.literal: At Zhenming's opening he was granted Deng prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenming he became military commissioner of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 會淮人圍安陸，彥卿奉詔領兵解圍，大破淮賊而回。

translations.literal: When Huai men besieged Anlu, Yanqing received edict and led troops to relieve the siege, greatly defeated Huai bandits and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan besieged Anlu he marched to the rescue, routed the Huai army, and returned.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒於鎮，時年五十七。

translations.literal: Year 4 he died in his post; at the time age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he died in office at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 詔贈侍中。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 彥卿貞幹明敏，善事人主，然怙寵作威，多忌好殺，雖顯立功名，而猶為識者之所鄙焉。

translations.literal: Yanqing was upright, capable, bright, and keen, good at serving his lord; yet relying on favor he wielded power, was much jealous and fond of killing; though he clearly established merit and fame, still he was despised by those with insight.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing was capable and shrewd in serving his prince, yet abused favor, was jealous and bloodthirsty, and despite his fame men of judgment held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：

translations.literal: The historiographer says:
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes:

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on lacuna in the historian's comment:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on lacuna in the historian's comment:

sentences.zh: （案：原本有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: The original text has lacunae.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The original is defective here.)〉

sentences.zh: 存敬有提鼓之勞，彥卿遇攀鱗之會，俱為藩後，亦其宜哉！

translations.literal: Cunjing had the merit of carrying the drum; Yanqing met the occasion of climbing the dragon scales; both became frontier defenders—also fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Cunjin had served at the drum; Yanqing caught the rise of the dragon; each became a frontier lord—as was only fitting!
